editorial:
Ever wonder what would happen if the king of zombie movies actually made the Resident Evil film? You get to dive deep into that exact question here. Director Brandon Salisbury gathers the people who were actually in the room when George A. Romero was planning his version of the game. It feels less like a boring history lesson and more like a mystery story. You get a front-row seat to the creative clashes and the wild ideas Romero had that would have made the movie totally different from the ones we got later on.

What really works is how the documentary keeps things moving quickly with great old footage and honest interviews. You will love seeing the original sketches and hearing why the project fell apart. The only downside is that you might feel sad that this movie never actually got made. If you are a gamer or a horror fan, you need to see this. It looks great streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but if you love movie history, you should definitely add the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the extra features.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing exactly where the deal broke down between Romero and the studio. It reveals that his vision was too slow and focused on social issues, which the bosses hated. The final scenes show a heartbreaking look at what could have been. It ends with a tribute to Romero, explaining that while the film died, his influence on the zombie genre lives on in every modern horror hit.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves zombie movies, Resident Evil games, or movie history.
